compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: We traveled from Horeb and went through all that great and terrible wilderness which you saw, by the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God…
observations.label: Text in view

observations.body: Moses recalls the route from Horeb to Kadesh Barnea.
observations.label: The route remembered

observations.body: Moses names the wilderness journey as the approach to a land Israel was told to take.
observations.label: Wilderness role

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 1:17–21 as its own wilderness scene before relating it to other journeys, memories, or visions.
payload.tension: The terrible road is behind them, but the decisive response at the land’s edge is still at issue.
payload.title: The great and terrible wilderness
